column1: # swiss-layout.tsv - the numbered launch layout `make swiss` exports.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Swiss shows a directory list, and the build directories
# are named for the source tree, not for a person standing in front of a
# television: `gbp-init-irq-program-probe` and `gbp-init-irq-deliver-probe`
# differ in one word in the middle, and a truncated list makes them look the
# same. Picking the wrong DOL wastes a physical run, so the operator-facing
# names live here, versioned, instead of being invented at export time.
# THE NUMBER IS AN OPERATIONAL INTERFACE. Once a build has a number it keeps it:
# a new POC takes the next free number and nothing is renumbered, so a written
# procedure stays valid. A retired number is never reused for a different test.
# Two digits always, because Swiss sorts lexically and `10-` sorts before `2-`.
# Ranges:
#   01-69   canonical POCs, in the order the research went
#   80-89   physical diagnostics: real builds, real runs, narrow questions
#   90-99   short-lived/special diagnostics
# Columns (tab separated):
#   number        two digits, unique, stable
#   short_name    the rest of the directory name; the whole `NN-short` stays short
#   source_poc    directory under poc/
#   dol           the launchable DOL, relative to build/poc/<out_dir>/
#   out_dir       directory under build/poc/ (differs from source_poc for variants)
#   make_target   what builds it (`build` for the ordinary POCs)
#   enabled       1 = exported, 0 = present but not exported
# The export copies the DOL byte for byte and verifies the hash; it never
# rewrites a build id, a commit or a single byte of the image. Authority stays
# with build/poc/<out_dir>/<dol>.
#number
